name: TIMES
aliases: Tolterodine and Tamsulosin in Men With LUTS Including OAB
question: Does tolterodine extended release plus tamsulosin improve perceived benefit and storage symptoms in men with LUTS and OAB compared with either drug alone or placebo?

design.population: Men aged at least 40 years with moderate-to-severe LUTS, bothersome bladder symptoms, and diary-documented frequency and urgency, with or without urgency urinary incontinence.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, four-arm superiority randomized trial
design.locator: JAMA article, Methods: Patients and Study Design; Results: Patient Disposition

verdictNote: Combination beat placebo on perceived benefit; the trial lasted 12 weeks.
takeaway: In men with LUTS and OAB, tolterodine ER plus tamsulosin improved week-12 patient-perceived benefit versus placebo; neither tolterodine ER nor tamsulosin alone significantly improved that primary outcome versus placebo after correction of a reported P value.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Kaplan SA, Roehrborn CG, Rovner ES, et al. "Tolterodine and tamsulosin for treatment of men with lower urinary tract symptoms and overactive bladder: a randomized controlled trial." *JAMA.* 2006;296(19):2319-2328. doi:10.1001/jama.296.19.2319

results.measure: Week-12 benefit; risk difference for combination versus placebo, percentage points
results.note: Protocol-specified analysis with last observation carried forward; 95% CI for risk difference is reported as rounded whole percentage points in Table 2. Corrected tamsulosin-placebo P=0.064; tolterodine-placebo P=0.48.
results.locator: JAMA article, Table 2 and Efficacy End Points; 2007 correction, p1864

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in episodes per 24 hours at week 12
results.note: Analyzed only among men with urgency urinary incontinence at baseline.
results.locator: JAMA article, abstract Results and Figure 2B

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in episodes per 24 hours at week 12
results.locator: JAMA article, abstract Results and Figure 2A

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in micturitions per 24 hours at week 12
results.locator: JAMA article, abstract Results and Figure 2C

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in micturitions per night at week 12
results.locator: JAMA article, abstract Results and Figure 2D

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in total IPSS at week 12
results.locator: JAMA article, abstract Results and Figure 3A

harms.label: Dry mouth
harms.note: Five combination recipients discontinued treatment because of dry mouth.

harms.label: Acute urinary retention requiring catheterization
harms.note: The combination recipient required catheterization after 4 days; the tolterodine recipient after 11 days.

harms.label: Change in postvoid residual volume
harms.note: Between-group changes were not statistically significant.

delivery.label: Daily drug regimen
delivery.value: Tolterodine ER 4 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, both, or matched placebo once daily for 12 weeks, about 30 minutes after dinner.

delivery.label: Medication adherence
delivery.value: More than 95% of the intention-to-treat population in each group ingested at least 80% of assigned medication.
delivery.locator: JAMA article, Results: baseline and adherence paragraph

reports.label: Tamsulosin P-value correction
reports.citation: "Incorrect Data in: Tolterodine and Tamsulosin for Treatment of Men With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and Overactive Bladder: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *JAMA.* 2007;298(16):1864. doi:10.1001/jama.298.16.1864
reports.followUp: Correction to the primary report; no new follow-up

reports.label: PSA subgroup analysis
reports.citation: Roehrborn CG, Kaplan SA, Kraus SR, et al. "Effects of serum PSA on efficacy of tolterodine extended release with or without tamsulosin in men with LUTS, including OAB." *Urology.* 2008;72(5):1061-1067. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2008.06.067
reports.followUp: Post hoc analysis of the original 12-week trial

results.measure: Post hoc changes in frequency, urgency sum, and IPSS storage by PSA stratum

values.exp: Improvement versus placebo in both PSA strata
values.tol: Improvement versus placebo only with PSA below 1.3 ng/mL
values.tam: No significant storage response in the lower-PSA stratum

results.note: Abstract reports statistical significance by stratum without effect sizes; baseline PSA was split at its median.
